title: When I need to report on content performance across platforms, I want to automatically aggregate ana
job_to_be_done: When I need to report on content performance across platforms, I want to automatically aggregate analytics from dev.to, Medium, and my personal blog into a single view, so I can avoid hours of manual data entry and get real-time insights.
painful_workflow: Manually exporting CSV from dev.to stats, copying data from other platforms, and reconciling in Excel for weekly or monthly reporting.
current_workaround: Export CSV from dev.to stats, copy data from other platforms, then manually reconcile in Excel.
verified_facts: The cluster is supported by exactly one signal (SIG-0002) from one source type (forum) with one independent source, per the cluster's own metadata.
The described workaround is manual: CSV export from dev.to, copying from other platforms, Excel reconciliation (SIG-0002).
The reporting cadence is weekly or monthly, not daily (SIG-0002).
No spend, paid tool, or consultant is mentioned anywhere in the evidence.
inferences: The 'hours spent every week' claim in SIG-0002 suggests real but modest labor cost, though the magnitude is unverified.
The target user (developer advocate) is technical and could likely automate much of this via dev.to's public API and standard analytics tools, reducing both pain and willingness to pay.
The JTBD's demand for 'real-time insights' is inconsistent with a weekly/monthly reporting trigger, suggesting the stated need may be aspirational rather than operational.
assumptions: That the single forum poster represents a broader population of developer advocates with the same workflow.
That the claimed time cost and error rates are accurate rather than exaggerated.
That multi-platform publishing (dev.to + Medium + personal blog) with formal reporting obligations is common enough to constitute a market.
unknowns: How many developer advocates actually publish across all three platforms AND must report on performance regularly.
Whether anyone has ever paid for a tool to solve this, or whether existing analytics/dashboard tools already cover it.
The actual hours spent per reporting cycle — no quantification exists in the evidence.
Whether the forum poster attempted and failed to self-solve with scripting, or simply hasn't tried.
Whether 'data entry errors' have ever caused a real consequence (bad decision, embarrassment, rework).
